name: Interlingua
variety: the Interlingua of the International Auxiliary Language Association (1951)
sources: Gode, Alexander & Blair, Hugh (1951). Interlingua: a Grammar of the International Language.
contrasts: five vowels with no length contrast
allophony: c before e, i is ts or s; r is a tap or trill

stress.rule: Stress falls on the vowel before the last consonant of the word; endings such as -le, -ne, -re and -ic- move it back.

rhythm.notes: No measurement exists: the class is what the design of the language implies.

intonation.declarative: not prescribed; speakers carry over the fall of their own languages
intonation.yes_no_question: rising at the end, as in the Romance languages
intonation.accent_shape: not prescribed; higher pitch on the stressed syllable is the usual practice
intonation.notes: The language has no native speakers whose melody could be described; what is given is the practice of its users.

notes: Pronunciation follows the Romance languages it is drawn from.
